drhp.business: OBSC Perfection manufactures precision metal components for a diversified set of end industries, including automotive, defence, marine and renewables. It reports a single operating segment, with India and outside India as its two geographical segments, and sells both domestically and through exports. Management describes the company as a supplier known for concurrent engineering and value engineering capabilities, serving OEM and Tier-1 customers.

Borrowings during the year were also used to fund capacity expansion — new plant & machinery, cold forging assets, and the Maharashtra and Gujarat land — and capital work-in-progress/capital advances rose for land acquisition and capacity expansion. risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Manufacturing relies on steel, aluminium and other metals; fluctuating commodity prices hit costs and margins, and pricing contracts or competition can prevent passing increases on to customers.
- Demand is tied to the automotive industry's health; any slowdown in vehicle production from downturns or policy changes directly affects order flows.
- Management flags that dependence on a concentrated set of OEM clients exposes the business to customer concentration risk.
- Export sales and import dependence for machinery or raw materials expose the Company to currency volatility.
- The industry has a large number of players competing for market share.
- Macro uncertainty, geopolitical conflicts or end-market slowdowns can hurt the auto and component industry for extended periods; managing supply-chain risk in an uncertain trade environment is flagged as a challenge.
- Increasing digitalisation (ERP, online ordering, supplier portals) exposes the Company to cyber threats and possible loss of designs, production data or customer information.
- Management notes a continuous need for capital investment in automation, quality upgrades and regulatory compliance. The Board states that no material risk has been identified other than general business risks.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversify from a currently automotive-dominated revenue base into newer industries such as defence, aerospace, marine and renewables
- Continue to grow export sales
- Expand the product portfolio, including EV and hybrid-compatible components
- Invest in automation and smart manufacturing (Industry 4.0)
- Build stronger relationships with OEMs and Tier-1 players
- Add further process capabilities — forging, stamping and eventually sub-assemblies — to move up the manufacturing value chain

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
